title: Completed constant realization of finite complexes and their reductions
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, and assume $P_n=A/I^n$ is finite for every $n$. Put $C=\varprojlim P_n$ and $J=IC$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $X$ be a scheme. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $\widehat A_X=\varprojlim\underline{P_n}$, using constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For a finite $C$-module $N$ put $c_X(N)=\varprojlim_n\underline{N/J^nN}$. The functor $c_X$ from finitely generated $C$-modules to sheaves of $\widehat A_X$-modules is exact and its values are adic lisse of finite type [def-weil-pbc-adic-lisse-module]. For a bounded complex $Q$ of finite $C$-modules, write $c_X(Q)$ for its termwise realization. Then there are natural isomorphisms
$$c_X(Q)\otimes^L_{\widehat A_X}\underline{P_n}\simeq\underline{Q\otimes_C^L P_n}$$
in the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], compatible with quotient transitions. For a scheme morphism $u:X\to T$, the same complex is a complex of $B=u^{-1}\widehat A_T$-modules via the projection-induced map $B\to\widehat A_X$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. There are natural isomorphisms
$$c_X(Q)\otimes_B^L u^{-1}\underline{(P_n)_T}\simeq\underline{Q\otimes_C^L P_n}_X.$$
These commute with all quotient reductions; no identification $u^{-1}\widehat A_T=\widehat A_X$ is asserted. Here derived tensors use K-flat resolutions as in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

source.place: Tag 09BV, lemma-weird, completed constant local models; agent exactness and derived realization argument using finite-module completion (algebra.tex Tag 00MB, lemma-completion-flat), pro-etale exact countable products, and the constant/completed scalar comparison of lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence

proof.text: First $C$ is Noetherian and $J$-adically complete, and its projection identifies $C/J^n$ with $P_n$ for every $n\geq1$, by the three cited completion results (a Noetherian ideal is finitely generated). A finite $C$-module $N$ is therefore $J$-adically complete and finitely presented. Its quotient $N/J^nN$ is finite as a set: a finite generating list gives a surjection from a finite power of the finite ring $C/J^n=P_n$.

Fix a site object $U$ and put $M_n=\underline{C/J^n}(U)$. Apply the constant-section properties over $C/J^n$: this ring is Noetherian since it is finite, and $M_n$ is flat over it. The same properties over $C$ make the quotient transitions surjective on sections. The limit-flat-modules theorem over $(C,J)$ now gives the canonical, natural identification
$$N\otimes_C\widehat A_X(U)\cong\varprojlim_n(N\otimes_C M_n)\cong\varprojlim_n\underline{N/J^nN}(U)=c_X(N)(U).$$
The second identification is the finitely presented tensor/sections assertion. These maps commute with restriction in $U$. Moreover that assertion with $M=C$ identifies $\underline N(U)$ with $\underline C(U)\otimes_C N$. Thus the presheaf tensor defining $\widehat A_X\otimes_{\underline C}\underline N$ has exactly the displayed sections and already is a sheaf. Sheafifying gives a natural $\widehat A_X$-linear isomorphism $c_X(N)=\widehat A_X\otimes_{\underline C}\underline N$, whose finite projections send $a\otimes x$ to $a_n\otimes(x\bmod J^nN)$.

Apply completed-constant-sheaf-reduction with coefficient ring $C$ and ideal $J$; its completed sheaf is $\widehat A_X$ by step 1. It is flat over $\underline C$. The constant-sheaf functor is exact by constant-module-section-properties, so the tensor identification of step 2 proves exactness of $c_X$. Also $I^nN=J^nN$, $N$ is complete, and $N/IN$ is finite over $A/I=C/J$. Hence the identity covering of $X$ and the module $N$, viewed as an $A$-module, give precisely the adic-lisse local model of the cited definition. No freeness of $N$ is used.

Here is a finite-free resolution for the entire bounded complex, rather than an assumption that an arbitrary K-flat resolution survives realization. Choose $b$ above its support, put $F^i=0$ for $i>b$, and construct $F^i$ and $f^i:F^i\to Q^i$ downwards. Given the higher terms, form
$$E^i=\{(q,k)\in Q^i\oplus F^{i+1}:d_Qq=f^{i+1}k,\ d_Fk=0\}.$$
It is a finite $C$-module by the Noetherian-submodule theorem. Choose a finite free module $F^i$ surjecting onto $E^i$ by the finite-free-resolution theorem, and define $f^i$ and $d_F^i$ by the two projections. The defining equations give $d_F^2=0$ and $d_Qf=fd_F$. A cocycle $q$ lifts using the pair $(q,0)$, and if a cocycle $k\in F^{i+1}$ maps to the boundary $d_Qq$, the pair $(q,k)$ lifts and makes $k$ a boundary. Thus $F\to Q$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Constant sheaves preserve it; exactness in step 3 shows $c_X(F)\to c_X(Q)$ is a quasi-isomorphism too. Each $c_X(F^i)$ is a finite sum of $\widehat A_X$, so this bounded-above complex is K-flat by the site K-flat theorem.

proof.text:
Compute derived reduction using the K-flat resolution $c_X(F)\to c_X(Q)$ of step 4 and derived pullback for the identity topos with coefficient map. In each degree, the projection gives
$$c_X(F^i)\otimes_{\widehat A_X}\underline{P_n}=\underline{F^i\otimes_C P_n},$$
since $F^i$ is finite free. The differential is a matrix over $C$, and its reduction on both sides is that same matrix modulo $J^n$; these degreewise maps therefore form a chain isomorphism. The module complex $F$ is K-flat by the module bounded-above-flat theorem, and $\underline{F\otimes_C P_n}$ represents $\underline{Q\otimes_C^L P_n}$ because constant sheaves are exact. This proves the first displayed isomorphism. The maps are canonical tensor/projection maps, natural on chain maps of resolutions. Derived tensor descent and the resolution-independence clause of derived pullback for the identity topos with coefficient map make the comparison independent of $F$ and natural in $Q$.

For the relative assertion, inverse image preserves constants: a constant sheaf of sets is a coproduct of copies of the terminal sheaf, and the left adjoint $u^{-1}$ preserves coproducts and the terminal object. Its preservation of finite limits and colimits makes it exact on abelian groups and modules; the constants comparison respects addition and scalar multiplication. Apply ringed-topos-flat-module-pullback to the flat $\underline C_T$-module $\widehat A_T$ and the coefficient isomorphism $u^{-1}\underline C_T=\underline C_X$. Thus $B=u^{-1}\widehat A_T$ is flat over $\underline C_X$. Apply the ordinary pullback/tensor isomorphism and exactness to the completed coefficient quotient at $T$ to get
$$B\otimes_{\underline C_X}\underline{P_n}_X\cong u^{-1}(\widehat A_T\otimes_{\underline C_T}\underline{P_n}_T)\cong u^{-1}\underline{P_n}_T=\underline{P_n}_X.$$
This is the projection-induced quotient map, and the map $B\to\widehat A_X$ respects it by its definition from these projections.

Put $H=\widehat A_X$ and $M=c_X(Q)$ with its restricted $B$-action. Choose a K-flat $B$-resolution $R\to M$. Because $B$ is flat over $\underline C_X$, restriction of $R$ is K-flat over $\underline C_X$: for every acyclic $\underline C_X$-complex $L$, $B\otimes_{\underline C_X}L$ is acyclic and
$$R\otimes_{\underline C_X}L=R\otimes_B(B\otimes_{\underline C_X}L)$$
is acyclic. Consequently the quotient isomorphism in step 6 gives
$$M\otimes_B^L\underline{P_n}_X\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\underline C_X}M\otimes_{\underline C_X}^L\underline{P_n}_X.$$
Indeed both sides are computed by $R\otimes_{\underline C_X}\underline{P_n}_X$, using $(r\otimes b)\otimes p\mapsto r\otimes bp$ and its inverse $r\otimes p\mapsto r\otimes(1\otimes p)$. Apply the finite-reduction comparison of constant-completion-equivalence to $(C,J,H,M)$, then step 5: the right side is $M\otimes_H^L\underline{P_n}_X\cong\underline{Q\otimes_C^L P_n}_X$. This proves the relative assertion without identifying $B$ with $H$.

proof.text: For $m\geq n$, write $q_{m,n}:P_m\to P_n$ for the quotient map. On a finite-free term in step 5 both orders of reduction send $a\otimes v$ to $q_{m,n}(a)\otimes v$. In step 2 both orders take $a\otimes x$ to $q_{m,n}(a_m)\otimes(x\bmod J^nN)$. In step 6 the projections defining $B\to H$ satisfy $q_{m,n}\pi_m=\pi_n$, also after inverse image. The balancing maps of step 7 send $(r\otimes b)\otimes p$ to $r\otimes bp$, and replacing $p$ by $q_{m,n}(p)$ gives $r\otimes bq_{m,n}(p)$ along either path. These identities commute with differentials and restrictions, hence with sheafification and derived localization. The constant-completion comparison already asserts compatibility with quotient transitions. This proves all the required commutative squares; the same formulas with three quotients give their cocycle identities.
